items.title: The Associations of Self-Determination and Cognitive Engagement with Vocational Students’ Critical Thinking Skills in a Gamified Learning Environment
items.abstract: A substantial body of previous research has examined gamification in educational settings, particularly its associations with self-determination, cognitive engagement, and critical thinking skills. However, there remain limitations in the analysis of gamification in relation to these constructs within vocational education. Therefore, this study was conducted to investigate the relationships among self-determination, cognitive engagement, and critical thinking skills in a learning process that incorporates gamification elements. A total of 309 students participated in this research and provided the data. The analysis was carried out using SmartPLS 3, applying Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) and Importance–Performance Map Analysis (IPMA). Based on the analytical results, there is a positive and significant relationship between self-determination and cognitive engagement. Furthermore, self-determination and cognitive engagement were positively associated with critical thinking skills. However, this study has limitations that should be acknowledged, as the data were obtained through self-report measures, which are subject to subjectivity and potential response bias. Therefore, future research is recommended to strengthen methodological rigor, both in terms of data collection and research approach, such as through qualitative studies and mixed-method designs.

items.title: THE COMPLEXITY GAP: AI IN STRATEGIC HCM
items.abstract: The transition from traditional Personnel Administration to Strategic Human Capital Management (HCM) redefines human assets from operational costs to the primary source of sustainable competitive advantage. However, executing this strategic vision in a post-pandemic environment presents unprecedented challenges. This theoretical paper systematically reflects upon the literature mapping the evolution of HCM. It applies the Resource-Based View (RBV) and the VRIO framework to analyze the synergistic impact of modern trends: Employee Experience (EX), organizational agility, continuous learning, and inclusion. The conceptual synthesis reveals that implementing these modern HCM imperatives creates a systemic "complexity gap." Organizations face a limitation of scalability, where the cognitive and analytical capacities of traditional management are overwhelmed by the need for hyper-personalization and massive data volumes. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is identified as a theoretical necessity rather than a mere technological upgrade. AI systems provide the augmented intelligence required to bridge the complexity gap. However, the paper critically highlights that this integration must navigate significant ethical risks, including algorithmic bias and privacy concerns, to ensure sustainable human-AI symbiosis.

items.title: The duality of playful work design: A diary study of designing fun and competition
items.abstract: Although employees often have limited control over task assignments, schedules, or collaboration partners, they may still have discretion in how they carry out tasks. Building on Job Demands-Resources theory, we integrate information-processing perspectives of play to propose that playful work design – proactively adding elements of fun and competition to routine activities – can be useful even in tightly structured jobs by increasing activated positive affect and reducing exhaustion. We tested this proposition in a 20-day diary study among 57 Norwegian naval cadets, yielding 1,046 day-level observations, using multilevel structural equation modeling. On days when cadets designed their work playfully, they reported more activated positive affect and less exhaustion. Combining designing fun with designing competition amplified these benefits. Thus, small discretionary choices in how employees approach work may produce immediate well-being gains in low-discretion roles and offer a micro-level pathway through which play at work can support performance.

items.title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Different Aspects of the Society
items.abstract: Abstract In recent times, artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a revolutionary transformative force in various sectors of the contemporary society. It has rapidly becomes an integral part of our daily lives. Now a days AI plays crucial role in transforming various aspects of society and generate new possibilities and opportunities. The paper also present a dissection of an impact of AI on different aspects of the society including agriculture, industry, education, market, finance, business, transportation, employment, healthcare etc. This article is presented in a narrative review. The main object of this research paper is an attempt to find and to analyze the positive and negative impact of artificial intelligence on various field of the society. This research paper provides a comprehensive overview of the impact of AI on various aspects of the society in the form of dynamic nature of economy, transformation in education system, modern and advanced healthcare system, change in nature of employment and ethics etc. The collected literature for this research paper is focused on socio-economic influence as well as future fear and challenges in implementing of AI. The AI related literature shows that it has large potential to provide significant benefits for the present modern society but it has also aware us about challenges and risk in implementing of AI technology. Because of many scientists, technologists and others concerned with the welfare of society have started fearing about the extensive use of AI and its impacts on the society. The medical field is more affected by use of AI technology. It plays a crucial role in diagnosis, surgery, appropriate treatment methods and other related healthcare services. It can also play an important role in education transforming with student personalized learning experience for student and teacher also. However, we cannot ignore some problems about using of AI in the field of viability of employment, economic inequality, and ethical issues. In short, this research paper provides a comprehensive overview of the impact of AI on various aspects of the present society life.

items.title: The Impact of Organizational Ergonomics on Job Burnout: Evidence from Higher Education Institutions in Iraq
items.abstract: This research aims to examine organizational ergonomics and its impact on job burnout among a random sample of teaching and administrative staff employed at universities, colleges, and institutes within higher education institutions in Iraq. This topic is of considerable importance because improving organizational ergonomics can enhance the work environment, increase job performance, and promote employee well-being. The research also seeks to address the problem of occupational stress and excessive workloads resulting from increasing teaching and administrative tasks assigned to employees in higher education institutions. These pressures contribute to higher levels of job burnout and adversely affect employee performance and job satisfaction. A descriptive-analytical approach was adopted, and data were collected using a structured questionnaire administered to a random sample of teaching and administrative staff. A total of 108 valid questionnaires. The data were analyzed using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) and the Analysis of Moment Structures (AMOS) program. The results showed a statistically significant positive correlation and influence between the two variables. This finding contradicts the prevailing theoretical trend in the literature. This result suggests the possibility of other organizational or psychological factors influencing this relationship within Iraqi higher education institutions. Accordingly, the study recommends that decision-makers in Iraqi higher education institutions should move beyond the mere implementation of ergonomic practices and adopt a comprehensive approach that integrates improvements to the physical work environment with psychological and social support, while proactively managing employee expectations to reduce job burnout and enhance organizational effectiveness.

items.title: The Legal and Ethical Challenges of Using Artificial Intelligence in Algeria
items.abstract: This study explores the legal and ethical problems arising from the integration of artificial intelligence technologies into the administrative and public-service systems of Algeria. It asks how far the country's existing legislative arsenal and its rules of digital ethics can absorb the accelerating development of intelligent systems, and assesses the role of the existing digital infrastructure in securing that transition. The paper adopts a descriptive-analytical methodology: the descriptive component inventories the relevant legal instruments and the available technical capacity, while the analytical component performs a gap analysis of whether texts drafted for classical digitisation can accommodate concepts such as the legal personality of a robot or liability for an algorithmic act, and subjects current digital administrative practice to critique against international ethical standards of transparency, fairness and non-discrimination. The study concludes that there is a clear legislative gap in the attribution of legal responsibility for algorithmic acts, particularly under the personal data protection legislation, because Algerian civil and criminal liability alike presuppose a discerning, willing human author whom an autonomous and opaque system does not supply. It further finds that the digital infrastructure, and specifically data centres and the national cloud, is the cornerstone of digital sovereignty and of ethical privacy, provided it is reinforced by an advanced cybersecurity framework and by reduced dependence on closed foreign platforms. The study recommends the drafting of a dedicated national legal framework and ethical charter for artificial intelligence, balancing technological innovation against the protection of the fundamental rights of the Algerian citizen.

items.title: The Moderating Effect of Digital Literacy on the Relationship between AI Interaction Quality and Consumer Emotional Engagement
items.abstract: As artificial Intelligence (AI) is having an increasing influence on the consumer-brand relationship, empirical evidence of the effects of AI-powered real-time communication on emotional brand engagement over time is scarce. Based on the Digital Emotional Brand Engagement (DEBE) model consisting of four outcome dimensions (Affective Engagement, Cognitive Engagement, Behavioral Engagement, Identification, and Emotional Attachment). The study proposes and empirically tests a model of four dimensions of AI interactions (Responsiveness and Availability, Personalization, Conversational Quality, Problem Resolution Efficiency). A descriptive-correlational quantitative design was adopted, and a sample of 400 consumers who had recently used AI-powered customer service was drawn. Multiple regression analysis and structural equation modeling (SEM) were used for analysis of the data, as well as mediation and moderation analysis (PROCESS macro). By considering all four dimensions of the interaction between people and artificial intelligence together, we could explain 52.1% of the variance in DEBE. The beta value for Affective Engagement was the largest for Responsiveness and Availability, while the highest beta value for Identification and Emotional Attachment was for Personalization. The overall path coefficient of the complete model from AI interaction to DEBE was 0.714. Partial mediation was observed between the quality of AI interaction and behavioral engagement with Identification and Emotional Attachment, and Digital Literacy had a significant moderating effect on the relationship between the quality of AI interaction and the emotional engagement of the consumer. The results highlight how critical an AI-powered customer service can be for boosting customers' emotional connection with brands in an e-marketing environment.

items.title: The Most Important Human Skills for the Age of AI and the Future of Work: FILE — The Five Intelligences of Leadership Evolution
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence changes what organizations can do; human leadership must decide what should be done, what remains accountable, and what must never be surrendered to machines. This working paper presents FILE: The Five Intelligences of Leadership Evolution as a human-centered management theory and diagnostic framework for responsible leadership and decision-making in the age of artificial intelligence and robotics. FILE argues that the most important human skills for the AI era and the future of work require the integrated exercise of five meta-intelligences: Augmented Intelligence, Emotional Intelligence, Cultural Intelligence, Political Intelligence, and Adaptive Intelligence. The paper defines the FILE formula, maps the framework onto the human hand, presents the 70 foundational nested intelligences, the 128-intelligence Teaching and Diagnostic Framework, and the 163-intelligence Extended Taxonomy, explains five emergent outcomes, and develops RC: The Relational Commons as the shared human ecosystem that leadership must protect, cultivate, and renew. It also clarifies boundaries among adjacent intelligences, offers a diagnostic application to AI-supported employee performance evaluation, and states limitations and future research directions. Its purpose is to establish a public, citable, and timestamped record of FILE as a transdisciplinary theory of human leadership in the age of AI and robots.

items.title: The revenue halo effect: How revenues and expenses asymmetrically affect perceptions of profitability
items.abstract: There are two primary ways to boost profits: increase revenues or decrease expenses. For example, whether a company increases revenues by $1 million or decreases expenses by $1 million, its profits will increase by $1 million (all else equal). But how do people subjectively evaluate such changes to revenues and expenses, and what inferences do they draw as a result? Across nine experiments ( N = 6045), an archival data analysis, and four supplemental studies, we document a robust “revenue halo” effect: increases in revenues, relative to equivalent decreases in expenses, lead to more positive perceptions of profitability, in both the short and long run, and result in more favorable overall impressions of financial strength, performance, potential, and trajectory. Consequently, managers who propose ideas for increasing revenues (vs. decreasing expenses) are viewed as more competent; consultants who develop such strategies are more likely to be rehired; and companies that report higher revenues are more attractive to investors. We furthermore propose that the revenue halo effect can be explained, in part, by the belief that strategies for increasing revenues are more innovative than strategies for decreasing expenses. Finally, to underscore the real-world relevance of our account, we analyze approximately 13 million financial news articles, finding that when firms reported increased revenues (vs. decreased expenses), they subsequently rose in Fortune 's “World's Most Admired Companies” rankings (the following year). This research identifies a novel asymmetry in judgments of organizational performance, with implications for managerial decision-making, corporate communication, and capital allocation.

items.title: THE ROLE OF AI TECHNOLOGIES IN DEVELOPING THE PROFESSIONAL COMPETENCE OF ENGLISH LANGUAGE TEACHERS
items.abstract: This article analyses the role of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in developing the professional competence of English language teachers, their pedagogical potential, and the methodological conditions required for their effective use. In contemporary education, the development of AI technologies is transforming the content of teachers’ professional activities and bringing such areas as lesson design, educational material development, personalised learning, assessment, feedback provision, and pedagogical reflection to a new level. Systematic studies published in 2026 indicate that language teachers are using generative AI (GenAI) technologies for lesson planning, the development of educational materials, and the support of writing activities; at the same time, they reveal competency needs related to AI literacy, technical skills, ethical decision-making, and data privacy. The article also proposes a pedagogical model for developing English language teachers’ competence in working with AI technologies. items.title: The Role of Conscious Leadership in Reducing Job Alienation: An Analytical Study of the Opinions of a Sample of Employees at the Presidency of Sulaimani Municipality
items.abstract: Background: Job alienation is an important organizational issue that may negatively affect employees’ attachment to their work. However, the actual level of job alienation and its relationship with conscious leadership remain unclear, creating a practical need for investigation. Objectives: This study aims to examine the relationship between conscious leadership and job alienation among employees at the Presidency of Sulaymaniyah Municipality, assess the statistical relationship between conscious leadership and job alienation, and determine which dimensions make significant predictive contributions to job alienation. Methods: The study adopted a descriptive-analytical approach. The study population comprised approximately 520 employees, and 250 questionnaires were distributed, 233 were returned, and 220 valid questionnaires were retained for analysis. Data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using SPSS version 25 through descriptive statistics, Cronbach’s alpha, Pearson’s correlation, and simple and multiple linear regression. Results: The findings showed that conscious leadership was perceived at a relatively high level, with Cognitive Awareness representing the most prominent dimension. Job alienation was at a relatively low to moderate level, with Normlessness being the most prominent dimension and Social Isolation the least prominent. A statistically significant negative relationship was found between conscious leadership and job alienation, and conscious leadership made a statistically significant negative contribution to the prediction of job alienation. At the dimensional level, Self-Awareness and Cognitive Awareness made statistically significant negative unique contributions, whereas Awareness of Others and Situational Awareness did not demonstrate statistically significant unique contributions. Conclusion: The findings indicate a statistically significant negative association between conscious leadership and job alienation. In particular, Self-Awareness and Cognitive Awareness made significant predictive contributions within the model, while the overall explanatory capacity remained limited, suggesting that other factors may also contribute to employees’ experiences of job alienation.

items.title: The safety and health plan for construction works: preventive planning tool or mere formal compliance
items.abstract: The construction sector is characterized by high organizational complexity derived from its temporary, dynamic, and process-specific nature. This industry registers some of the highest occupational accident rates worldwide. Within the European regulatory framework, Directive 92/57/EEC establishes the Health and Safety Plan (H&SP) as the principal instrument for preventive management on-site. In Spain, the transposition of this Directive introduced a preliminary design-phase document (Health and Safety Study or Basic Study, H&SS/H&SBS), intended to identify risks and define preventive measures that subsequently inform the contractor’s H&SP. Despite the importance of H&SS/H&SBS documents within the safety management process, empirical evidence remains limited regarding both their technical quality and their predictive capacity to explain the quality of subsequent H&SPs. This study addresses this gap through a qualitative and quantitative approach aimed at evaluating the intrinsic quality of H&SS/H&SBS and H&SP documents and modelling the dependency relationship between them. A database comprising 560 documents (280 H&SS/H&SBS and 280 H&SP) from 280 construction projects was assessed using a Delphi-based expert evaluation tool combined with a ratio weighting method. The results reveal consistently low levels of document quality and a limited capacity of H&SS/H&SBS to predict the quality of the corresponding H&SP. These findings suggest a systemic “cascade” failure in preventive planning, whereby documents frequently operate as instruments of formal compliance rather than as effective safety management tools. Our models’ findings support the need for effective audits and advanced technical training for professionals drafting these documents to improve preventive planning.

items.title: The Transformasi Proses Belajar pada Era Generative Artificial Intelligence: Sintesis Konseptual tentang Cognitive Offloading, Keterlibatan Kognitif, dan Integritas Akademik
items.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used by university students not only to locate information, but also to explain concepts, organize ideas, and complete academic tasks. This article examines the psychological processes that may explain why such use can support learning in some situations while reducing students' intellectual involvement in others. A conceptual literature review was conducted by bringing together foundational work on Distributed Cognition, Extended Mind, Cognitive Load, Student Engagement, and the ICAP Framework with recent studies on GenAI in education. Sources were selected for their relevance to cognitive offloading, cognitive engagement, and academic integrity. The review suggests that the educational consequences of GenAI depend less on its mere use than on how cognitive work is divided between students and the system. Offloading routine demands may free resources for evaluation and reflection, whereas delegating core reasoning may weaken engagement and make academic products less representative of students' own understanding. On this basis, the Educational Cognitive Transformation Model (ECTM) is proposed to connect learning transformation, cognitive offloading, redistribution of cognitive activities, cognitive engagement, learning quality, and academic integrity. ECTM is offered as a conceptual proposition that still requires empirical testing.

items.title: The Use of AI Software in Reviewing Applicants for General Surgery Residency
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools are increasingly used to improve efficiency, including in residency application review. While these technologies may streamline processes, their ability to identify optimal candidates for specific programs remains uncertain. This study aims to evaluate if AI can enhance the productivity of residency application review without compromising selection quality. METHODS: General surgery residency applications were analyzed using a large language model-based AI platform configured with customized program-specific weighting of applicant metrics. The AI-generated scores and rank list were compared with results from the traditional review process in which the application review committee manually reviews applications, scores applicants, and selects candidates for interview. RESULTS: A total of 847 applications were reviewed, and 96 applicants were manually selected (MS) for interviews by the application review committee. Of these, 32 (33%) were also ranked in the AI's top 96 candidates, including 7 in the top 10. Quartile analysis demonstrated that 51 (53.1%) MS candidates were in the top quartile of AI rankings, 26 (27.1%) in the second, 8 (8.3%) in the third, and 11 (11.4%) in the bottom. Adjusting the weights of various factors did not significantly alter these distributions. Technical review revealed scoring anomalies, including negligible AI scores for some candidates selected for interview. Analysis of the weighted factors showed that letters of recommendation contributed 29.4% of MS vs 25.1% of AI scoring (p = 0.009), research 6.3% vs 8.0% (p = 0.017), MSPE 7.4% vs 9.0% (p = 0.073), and factors such as USMLE and experiences were equivalent between the 2 groups. CONCLUSION: AI-assisted review may serve as a useful adjunct for initial screening but requires further refinement and training to better replicate human qualitative judgment. Future work will include evaluating concordance between AI rankings and the final program rank list and additional application review to guide software optimization and improve reliability as a screening tool.

items.title: The use of ergonomics methods in logistics process - case study
items.abstract: Ergonomics, as a scientific discipline, is gaining increasing importance in modern workplaces, as people spend more time engaged in work-related activities, often in static postures and under continuous technological exposure. Ergonomics focuses on adapting working conditions to match the physical and mental capabilities of humans, with the primary goals of enhancing productivity, ensuring safety, and improving overall employee well-being. Proper ergonomic practices help prevent workplace injuries, reduce fatigue, and create a healthier and more efficient work environment. One of the key roles of ergonomics is to reduce human fatigue during work processes. By designing tasks, tools, and workspaces that align with human capabilities, ergonomics minimizes unnecessary physical and mental strain. This not only improves worker comfort and health, but also contributes to clearer and more realistic standards for performing operations. As a result, ergonomics plays a vital role in increasing labor productivity and maintaining long-term efficiency in production environments. The emergence of new Industry 4.0 technologies such as automation, digitization, and artificial intelligence presents additional challenges for ergonomics. These rapid technological advancements require ongoing ergonomic adaptations to ensure safe, healthy, and sustainable work practices. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the field of ergonomics and presents key ergonomic methods. Special attention is given to the software solution ErgoFellow 3.0, which includes various tools to assess and implement ergonomic improvements. The use of computer-aided ergonomics enables quick, accurate evaluations of working conditions, supporting a safer and more productive workplace.

items.title: THE VICIOUS CYCLE OF DIGITAL ESCAPISM: A LITERATURE REVIEW ON ONLINE GAMING ADDICTION, OCCUPATIONAL BURNOUT AND PRODUCTIVITY AMONG YOUNG ADULT PROFESSIONALS
items.abstract: Introduction: Occupational burnout among young adult professionals has reached concerning levels, and there are more people struggling with internet gaming disorder (IGD) each day. Studies suggest these two problems feed into each other. Burnout can drive people toward gaming as an escape, and gaming can reduce work performance, which in turn increases burnout. This literature review was conducted to discuss how occupational burnout, gaming addiction, and work performance relate to one another among young professionals. Methods: We searched the MEDLINE, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases from 2001 to 2025. Results: We included 52 relevant studies, and the findings show that each part of the cycle reinforces the others. Burnout increases escapism behaviors (r = 0.31-0.65), and escapism motivation is the strongest predictor of IGD among gaming motivations (r = 0.40); it also bridges the relationship between work stress and pathological gaming. Discuss: Most of the studies conclude that a vicious cycle exists where burnout could become gaming addiction through digital escapism, and gaming addiction decreases work productivity and then leads back into burnout. Digital escapism appears to be a crucial link in the chain. Addressing these problems requires intervention at multiple levels, organizational changes alongside individual support. Longitudinal research testing actual interventions would be a valuable next step. Conclusion: Growing interdependence between digital wellness and occupational health necessitates coordinated, multilevel interventions targeting individual, behavioral, organizational, and structural determinants. Given the substantial individual and economic burden, greater investment in longitudinal research, policy development, and rigorously evaluated interventions is essential.

items.title: Towards Proactive Medication Safety: Artificial Intelligence-Based Prediction, Detection, and Prevention of Drug-Related Problems in Clinical Practice
items.abstract: Abstract Background Medication-related problems, including adverse drug reactions (ADRs), adverse drug events (ADEs), drug–drug interactions (DDIs), medication errors, and inappropriate antimicrobial use, remain important challenges in clinical practice. Artificial intelligence (AI) has developed rapidly and may help healthcare professionals identify medication-related risks earlier. Previous studies have reported the use of machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, and newer generative AI methods in pharmacovigilance, drug-interaction prediction, clinical decision support, and antimicrobial stewardship. Objective This study aimed to review AI's role in predicting, detecting, and preventing drug-related problems and to compare its applications across pharmacovigilance, drug–drug interaction prediction, clinical decision support, medication safety, and antimicrobial stewardship. Methods We conducted a literature review of 39 selected articles on AI and medication safety. The literature was organised into major areas, including ADR/ADE prediction and pharmacovigilance, DDI prediction, clinical decision support, generative AI and EHR-based medication safety applications, and antimicrobial stewardship. The findings were compared according to AI methods, clinical purpose, safety application, benefits, and major limitations. Results The reviewed literature shows that AI can analyse large amounts of clinical and medication data to identify patients at risk of ADRs and ADEs, detect possible DDIs, support medication decisions, and improve pharmacovigilance. Machine learning and deep learning methods have shown promising results in prediction and classification tasks. AI has also been used to support antibiotic selection, antimicrobial resistance prediction, and antimicrobial stewardship. Generative AI and large language models are emerging in DDI identification, clinical decision support, and pharmacovigilance. However, most studies remain retrospective, and external validation and prospective clinical testing are still limited. Conclusion AI has strong potential to support a proactive medication-safety system by predicting risks, detecting problems early, and supporting preventive action. However, AI should support rather than replace healthcare professionals. Future research should focus on high-quality data, external validation, explainable AI, patient privacy, clinical integration, and real-world testing. The ultimate goal should be to develop safe, reliable, and patient-centred AI systems that help reduce medication-related harm and improve clinical outcomes. items.title: Tracing the Path from Self-Efficacy to Artificial Intelligence Use: The Mediating Role of Technology Acceptance Among Mathematics Undergraduates in Nigeria
items.abstract: The way students learn, engage with, and create information has changed as artificial intelligence (AI) becomes more common in classrooms. Therefore, understanding the factors that influence students' adoption of AI tools is vital to improving learning outcomes, especially in disciplines that require extensive mathematics. This study examined the mediating role of technology acceptance in the relationship between self-efficacy and AI use among mathematics undergraduates in Nigeria. We used a quantitative cross-sectional design and collected data from 256 students across three public universities in Southwestern Nigeria using a structured survey instrument. We operationalised technology acceptance solely as perceived ease of use, rather than as the full set of constructs typically represented in the Technology Acceptance Model. Data were analysed using PLS-SEM. The findings showed that self-efficacy significantly and positively relates to both technology acceptance (β = 0.591, t = 9.166, p < .05, f² = 0.537) and AI use (β = 0.301, t = 4.727, p < .05, f² = 0.092). Technology acceptance also significantly relates to AI use (β = 0.371, t = 5.093, p < .05, f² = 0.140) and partly mediated the relationship between self-efficacy and AI use. The model explained 35.0% of the variance in technology acceptance (R² = 0.350) and 36.1% of the variance in AI use (R² = 0.361), while both endogenous constructs demonstrated predictive relevance (Q² > 0). The findings suggest that mathematics educators can support AI use by strengthening students’ technological self-efficacy and ensuring that AI tools are easy to use within mathematics learning activities. Theoretically, the findings indicate that perceived ease of use provides an important mechanism through which self-efficacy relates to students’ AI use, while also highlighting the need to distinguish this specific acceptance dimension from broader technology acceptance models.

items.title: Triarchic corrigibility: a role-separated governance design pattern for AI-assisted decision-making
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) alignment is often framed as the problem of making a model reliably pursue human intentions or values. That work is indispensable, but deployed systems also raise a governance problem: who controls information, private context, correction, escalation, and action? This conceptual article proposes triarchic corrigibility as a role-separated governance design pattern for AI-assisted decision-making. The pattern combines (1) an embodied and answerable human, or an accountable human decision body; (2) a strictly isolated local AI layer for private contextual continuity; and (3) an externally connected AI layer for current public-world evidence. Final authorization of consequential action remains human, while epistemic and procedural competences are deliberately distributed so that no component can unilaterally control framing, memory, procedure, and execution. The article specifies a normative basis, trust-domain separation, decision rights, human-mediated data flows, reciprocal challenge, escalation, affected-party recourse, proportionate audit, and exit procedures. It distinguishes personal and organizational instantiations, compares the pattern with single-assistant, local-only, edge–cloud, multi-agent, human-in-the-loop, meaningful-human-control, and polycentric approaches, and provides criteria and rejection conditions for evaluating its value. It also advances an evolutionary-symbiotic hypothesis: repeated, bounded dependence on complementary roles may make correction and cooperative continuity preferable to unilateral control while preserving interruption, replacement, and exit. A worked case illustrates the protocol. The result is a testable governance hypothesis whose capacity to reduce correlated failure, preserve privacy and human judgment, and sustain correction under residual uncertainty requires empirical evaluation.

items.title: Trust and Continuance Intention Toward AI-Powered Research Tools: The Moderating Role of Transparency Framing Style
items.abstract: As AI becomes more deeply embedded in scientific workflows, understanding what drives user trust has become central to the sustainable adoption of these tools. This study draws on the Ability-Benevolence-Integrity (ABI) model to examine what shapes trust in AI-powered research tools and how that trust relates to users’ intention to continue using them. A key contribution is the introduction of Transparency Framing Style (TFS) as a novel construct. Whereas transparency refers broadly to how much information an AI system discloses about its data, reasoning and limitations, TFS concerns how that information is structured, emphasised and worded when presented to users. Data were collected from 274 academics and postgraduate researchers across 10 Malaysian universities using purposive sampling and analysed through partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). The structural model explains 68.6% of the variance in trust and 39.8% in continuance intention. Among the ABI dimensions, integrity showed a larger estimated association with trust (β = 0.251, p < 0.001) than benevolence (β = 0.081, p = 0.047). TFS was the strongest direct predictor of trust (β = 0.531, p < 0.001) and positively moderated the relationship between trust and continuance intention (β = 0.180, p < 0.001). These findings extend the human-AI interaction literature by highlighting the importance of interpretive compatibility alongside technical competence in sustaining engagement with AI-powered research tools.

items.title: Trust Is Not a Score: Runtime Assurance Contracts for High-Risk AI Agents
items.abstract: Benchmarks, audits, and agent protocols describe performance, permissions, and repair, but not how observed evidence should change an agent's authority during a consequential task. We call this the assurance-transition gap. We propose a Runtime Assurance Contract (RAC), a policy-level formal schema binding autonomy boundaries, component eligibility, evidence state, transition policy, human-review capacity, and non-compensatory gates. Under RAC, soft metrics may inform routing, whereas a failed or unknown mandatory gate forces retry, switch, escalation, deferral, or stop; aggregate performance cannot authorize action. We define the contract, an evidence record, a permission rule, and five invariants, and illustrate them in clinical, industrial, and judicial failure probes. We then report a deterministic failure-injection study in agentic coding: 280 constructed cases evaluated by a gate conjunction, a score-only rule, and a restricted protocol baseline. At the published example weights and threshold, the score rule admits 80 of 100 block-required injections and all 40 review-required injections. Tuned in hindsight, it matches the conjunction on this corpus. For positive weights, a positive threshold, binary risk signals, zero-signal controls, and an injected case firing each signal alone, we show that exact agreement holds if and only if the threshold does not exceed the smallest weight. A separate set of 18 hand-authored traces checks version-pinned evidence and review transitions against simpler policy variants. In a further prospective synthetic holdout of 24 episodes, two blinded LLM judges assign identical labels to all 72 action attempts; RAC and a separately implemented full stateful baseline both match these labels. These studies test mechanisms on synthetic cases; they establish neither deployed safety nor cross-domain effectiveness.

items.title: Trustworthy agricultural autonomy integrates robot learning safe control and human robot interaction
items.abstract: The future of modern farming is intelligent, autonomous and data-driven farming operations. This will help to address the increasing labor shortage, resource constraints and climate variability. But for deployment in unstructured agricultural settings, high-performance automation is needed, as well as trustworthy systems that can make safe decisions, have the ability to learn adaptively and collaborate effectively with human operators. In this review, we discuss recent progress in trustworthy agricultural autonomy from the perspective of three interrelated pillars: robot learning and perception, safe control and resilient planning, and human-robot interaction. This review surveys state-of-the-art perception technologies such as computer vision, LiDAR, sensor fusion and deep reinforcement learning and safety-oriented approaches including model predictive control, formal verification, failure management and resilient navigation. It also addresses human-robot collaborative systems, explainable AI, ergonomics safety and sustainability-aware robotic design and discusses ethical, regulatory and socio-economic issues related to autonomous farming. Commercial applications of autonomous weeding, robotic harvesting and broad-acre field operations are now in existence, providing real-world demonstrations of the use of these technologies, and their potential to increase productivity, improve resource efficiency and enhance environmental sustainability. Finally, the review wraps up by underlining some future research priorities like universal safety certification, edge computing, interoperability, swarm robotics, and digital twin integration. Collectively, the reviewed evidence identifies the technical, human, and governance requirements that must be addressed to support safer, more resilient, transparent, and sustainable deployment of autonomous agricultural systems. items.title: Turning Free-to-Use Generative AI into Flipped-Interaction Intelligent Tutors: Exploring Student Engagement and Perceptions of Learning
items.abstract: Abstract An engaging and cost-effective digital tool for developing subject-matter knowledge (SMK) could mitigate educational inequities in resource-constrained contexts. This case study explores the effectiveness of free generative artificial intelligence (GAI) platforms, prompted to function as a Flipped-Interaction Intelligent Tutoring System (FIITS), to promote science student-teacher SMK learning. Data were collected across a 10-week intervention from 42 third- and fourth-year natural and physical sciences student teachers at two campuses of a South African university. The students engaged with the FIITS in odd-numbered weeks by pasting a provided prompt into a free GAI platform, and with benchmarking interactive electronic worksheets in even-numbered weeks. Affective, behavioural, and cognitive engagement and perceptions of SMK learning were analysed using post-session questionnaires, end-of-module reflections, and group interviews. Both modalities elicited consistently high and comparable engagement levels, but students reported stronger perceptions of SMK development with the FIITS. They valued its personalisation, relevance, and human-like interactivity, although workload pressures and occasional GAI errors somewhat hindered the FIITS’s effectiveness. These findings suggest that free GAI platforms, prompted to behave as FIITS, may provide equitable, scalable, and pedagogically effective tools for improving SMK in student-teacher education. Recommendations include scaffolding an initial adjustment phase, incorporating varied levels of challenge, and managing novelty and workload to sustain engagement. This study offers early evidence of the pedagogical potential of free flipped-interaction GAI in science teacher education, particularly in contexts where access to costly educational technologies is limited.

items.title: Two pathways at once: An investigation of how reactance and ethicality shape student learning with AI
items.abstract: Generative AI tools promise to expand student agency in management education, yet the same tool can help and hurt learning inside a single classroom. We argue this contradiction is the signature of two psychological pathways running in parallel. Drawing on the cognitive-affective-conative framework, we develop a dual-pathway serial mediation model in which a cognitive pathway runs from psychological reactance through autonomy perceptions to effectiveness judgments, while an affective pathway runs from ethical perceptions through emotional engagement to effectiveness judgments. Ninety-seven undergraduate management students participated in two AI-enhanced activities with different chatbot tools across one semester. Both pathways operated as predicted. More surprising was how the cognitive pathway changed across exposures. At first use, reactance traveled through autonomy, consistent with self-determination theory. By the second activity, reactance bypassed autonomy and suppressed effectiveness directly. The affective pathway remained stable across exposures. For management educators, ethical framing before a student's first AI encounter may do more work than redesigning the tools themselves to preserve student choice. As a single-cohort study using two researcher-built chatbots, the results are preliminary and point to hypotheses for multi-site replication rather than population estimates.

items.title: Using interactive immersive simulations and digital analytical records to improve cadets' decision-making and situational awareness
items.abstract: The rapid adaptation of future specialists to extreme conditions of professional activity highlights the relevance of introducing interactive simulations for realistic modeling of scenario-oriented didactic situations. The study assesses the pedagogical effectiveness of interactive simulation training in developing decision-making, situational awareness, and team interaction skills among cadets. The following methods were used for this purpose: focused search, comparative analysis, and effectiveness assessment. Empirical verification based on a sample of 64 cadets showed a significant improvement in the development dynamics of key indicators of professional training in the experimental group. The integral time of task completion decreased by 54%, the speed of cognitive reaction increased by 67%, and the accuracy of target actions (error minimization) increased by 46%. This study demonstrates a novel comprehensive pedagogical analysis of interactive simulations based on technical and functional characteristics and the integral parameter of readiness. Further research should focus on expanding the sample of participants to increase the statistical reliability of the results, as well as on analyzing a wider range of interactive technologies to determine their effectiveness in various professional scenarios.

items.title: Vigitalization: The Sociotechnical Configuration of Structural Surveillance and Algorithmic Governance in the Digital Anthropocene
items.abstract: Contemporary society faces the ubiquitous proliferation of algorithmic systems that structure social life, from intimate subjective modulation to planetary crisis management. This conceptual paper therefore proposes the analytical category of vigitalization. Rooted in relational sociology, vigitalization is defined as a co-constitutive sociotechnical configuration that fuses datafication with structural surveillance to interpret the autonomization of algorithmic governance. Employing a multilevel theoretical framework bridging the macro (systematicity), meso (grouping), and micro (interaction) dimensions, the study dissects the relational interdependencies between technological infrastructures, political economy, and algocratic bureaucracies. Vigitalization operates under a strict recursive logic: digitizing to monitor and monitoring to digitize, naturalizing behavioral extraction across all institutional boundaries. Crucially, this framework positions vigitalization as the primary sociotechnical matrix governing the ASAM Nexus (Agency-Structure-Algorithm-Matter). By doing so, it equips sociology with the critical apparatus required to address the existential macro-risks, biopolitical subsumption, and biometric enclosures intrinsic to the Digital Anthropocene.

items.title: Virtual Learning Environments in Organizational Trainings: Unlocking its Potential
items.abstract: Abstract: This study investigates the evolving role of Virtual Learning Environments (VLEs) in organizational training. We use PRISMA approach to conduct a systematic literature review (SLR) to investigate the importance of VLE. It compiles study findings on VLEs, e-learning, and organizational learning. Training environments, learning criteria, professional training techniques, and training results are the major themes identified in this article. The study highlights challenges and opportunities associated with VLE implementation. It contributes to the discourse on workplace learning, underscoring the pivotal role of VLEs in enhancing organizational performance and employee development. Results underscore the increasing focus that businesses are placing on VLEs, stressing advantages and tackling implementation related obstacles, and extensive examination of VLE adoption. The research advances knowledge about how businesses can successfully integrate VLE procedures. The authors conclude emphasizing the strategic benefits of VLEs, suggesting avenues how businesses can successfully integrate VLE. This research is confined to the boundaries of employee performance and satisfaction. items.title: When Digital Hindrance Stressors Lead to Cyberloafing: Insights from Self-regulation Theory
items.abstract: With the continuous advancement of digital transformation, digital technologies such as big data and artificial intelligence have greatly reshaped corporate office practices. While these technologies significantly improve organizational work efficiency, they also produce digital hindrance stressors, which bring negative effects on employees’ mental states and work behaviors. In digital office settings, employees are faced with growing digital‑related work pressure, and cyberloafing as a type of work‑deviant behavior occurs more frequently. Drawing on self‑regulation theory, this study selects self‑regulation impairment as the mediating variable and self‑regulation trait as the moderating variable. It systematically analyzes the underlying influence path through which digital hindrance stressors act on employees’ cyberloafing behavior via self‑regulation impairment, under the moderating effect of self‑regulation trait.

items.title: When the Feed Feels Personal: Emotional Dependency on Social Media Algorithms
items.abstract: DOI : https://doi.org/10.82471/qem0g-t6g81 This paper explores the emotional dependence on algorithmic feeds in the everyday social media use. Using qualitative data from a phenomenological study of internet users in Kerala, this research analyses how users experience and make sense of algorithmic recommendations in their everyday emotional contexts. The study goes beyond the usual questions on algorithmic awareness or technical understanding. It looks at how individual feeds become relevant through moods, rituals, vulnerabilities and everyday interpretations. It implies that users’ interactions with algorithms are not only shaped by visibility but also by affective experiences. The research claims that emotional dependence on algorithms is not an issue of overuse, but rather a negotiated interaction between algorithmic personalisation and user affective interpretations, foregrounding user narratives. items.title: Why and what do students want to learn about AI? Investigating motivations and learning interests among undergraduates across disciplines
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are now widely applied across different domains. As AI systems increasingly shape professional and academic domains, there is a growing need to pre-pare future professionals to work with these technologies responsibly and effectively. Accordingly, an increasing number of studies advocate AI education for undergraduates across disciplines. However, there is limited qualitative research on these students’ motivations for learning about AI and on what they are interested in learning, despite the importance of such understanding for designing motivating, engaging, and effective learning experiences. Therefore, the objective of this research is to answer the following two research questions: (1) What motivates undergraduates across disciplines to learn about AI? (2) What are undergraduates across disciplines interested in learning about AI? To answer the research questions, we conducted a survey with 128 students who voluntarily enrolled in an elective introductory AI course over three semesters. The findings indicate that these students are motivated to learn about AI not only for career-related utility but also due to its perceived societal relevance and ethical implications. Regarding learning interests, students most frequently expressed interest in learning how AI systems work, how these systems impact society positively and negatively, and how to use them effectively and responsibly. In the discussion section, we provide guidance on how these results can inform the design or adaptation of AI curricula, course invitations, and learning experiences to foster sustained engagement and meaningful learning among these students.

items.title: Workplace learning in civil-military crisis exercises: constructive alignment, context support and defensive routines
items.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine how constructive alignment, context support, psychological safety and defensive routines are associated with observable indicators of workplace learning in civil-military crisis exercises and why exercise participation should not be equated with demonstrated learning. Design/methodology/approach This study is a comparative qualitative reanalysis of two previously studied Swedish exercise settings conducted between 2022 and 2024. No new empirical data was collected for this study. The structurally nonequivalent cases are compared using the same deductive workplace-learning framework; the comparison is used to elaborate theory rather than to estimate causal effects. Findings Case A exhibited more observable indicators of learning progression, along with clearer objectives, sequenced activities, feedback opportunities and stronger contextual support. Case B displayed fewer such indicators alongside vague objectives, limited assessment, heterogeneous participant experience and recurring defensive routines. Because the cases also differ in duration, immersion, group stability, participant composition and unit of analysis, these patterns are interpreted as associations rather than causal effects of exercise design. Research limitations/implications The comparison concerns one five-day exercise and a composite of seven exercises, uses unequal qualitative corpora and lacks independent pre- and postmeasures or behavioral evidence of transfer. This study therefore identifies theoretically relevant patterns and observable learning-process indicators, not verified individual learning outcomes or causal effects. Practical implications Exercise planners should connect specific learning objectives to role-relevant activities and structured feedback, while deliberately providing legal expertise, role clarity, facilitation and conditions for speaking up. Evaluation should distinguish immediate exercise outputs from subsequent transfer to ordinary work. Originality/value This study does not add new empirical data. Its contribution is a standardized cross-case reanalysis that integrates constructive alignment with workplace-learning affordances, psychological safety, defensive routines and training-transfer research and specifies the boundary conditions under which exercise outputs can be interpreted as indicators of learning progression.

items.title: Worse Together: How Performance Breaks Down in Multi-User Multi-Agent Teams
items.abstract: People are increasingly delegating tasks to AI agents, and those agents are increasingly encountering other people's agents over shared resources such as a codebase, a calendar, or a budget. When each agent acts for a different user with different goals, coordination often fails, and the group ends up worse off than if a single agent had acted for everyone. We study this multi-user, multi-agent setting across five frontier models and 77 scenarios in four environments: an API key environment in which agents share a compute budget, a clinic in which they share a calendar, a personal assistant environment in which they share a group order or booking, and a merge queue in which they share a release cutoff. In each scenario, we compare a single agent that serves every user (a coordinator) to a team in which each agent serves one user, with and without a communication channel between the agents. Teams deliver worse group outcomes than the coordinator in every environment: without a channel, they completely collapse in two environments, and even with one, coordination overhead creates substantial gaps. For example, in the personal assistant environment, the coordinator fulfills a targeted user request about twice as often as teams. We identify distinct behaviors associated with this poor group-level performance, including stalling as teams grow, overriding each other's actions, and fabricating claims. We find effective but environment-specific mitigations, such as a team lead, explicit procedural instructions, and a platform check that makes an agent read its peers' messages before committing. We will release the API key, clinic, and personal assistant environments as MAMUBench, comprising 74 scenarios for evaluating multi-user, multi-agent coordination.

items.title: Writing with the Machine: Negotiating Authorial Identity in AI-Assisted Academic Writing Practices among Post-Graduate Students
items.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) has revolutionized academic writing, shifting the nature of human-AI interactions in text production. While previous studies focus on academic honesty and general writing outcomes, little research addresses how multilingual university students negotiate authorial identities during AI integration. This qualitative study explores the negotiation of authorial identity among 15 postgraduate students at Mahendra Multiple Campus, Tribhuvan University, Nepal, using semi-structured interviews and reflexive thematic analysis. Guided by Ivanič’s Writer Identity Theory, Vygotsky’s Sociocultural Theory, Norton’s Identity and Investment Theory, and Bourdieu’s Linguistic Capital Theory, the study investigates students' perceptions of authorship, creativity, and linguistic voice. Empirically, the findings reveal five key outcomes: (1) students utilize GenAI primarily as a linguistic scaffolding tool to bridge conceptual ideas and formal academic English; (2) authorship is experienced as a negotiated sociotechnical space where intellectual ownership of ideas remains human while linguistic expression is co-constructed; (3) GenAI acts as a cognitive and creative partner that stimulates alternative argumentation rather than replacing human ingenuity; (4) participants experience an internal tension between achieving polished Western-centric academic English and preserving their authentic multilingual voices; and (5) sustainable writing relies on robust human agency, critical evaluation, and editorial oversight. These findings demonstrate that AI is not a mere substitution tool but an intervening mediator that reshapes scholarly writing. The study offers critical insights from a South Asian multilingual higher education context, advocating for AI-literate classrooms that foster intellectual ownership while enabling responsible technological utilization.
